text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the summary is cautious and flags thin documentation. Several statements are inaccurate or inconsistent, though: the rash claim, the 'lean' contradiction, the 'two to three times in every band' claim, and a comparison figure that does not match the card. The next steps are generic and do not name the specific claims or the key follow-up.","problems":["Cites C0084532 as 'rash', but the card shows dx R21 only; the card does not name the diagnosis, so the label is an unsupported interpretation. R21 is the ICD-10 code for rash, so this may be fine, but the summary also labels C0084474 as an upper respiratory infection (J06.9), which is acceptable.","Says the billing pattern 'points toward upcoding more than toward panel acuity' while the leaning is 'inconclusive' and the headline says records are too few; the stance is internally inconsistent.","Claims the 99215 share is 'roughly two to three times the all-provider rate in every complexity band'; the card ratios are 2.3, 2.3, 2.7, 2.7, 2.7, 1.8, so the 5+ band is under 2x and the claim is overstated.","Compares 0% below billed against '14% for comparison providers', but the card's all-provider rate is 14.3% for 99215 only and it is unclear whether that is a below-billed rate; this is a weak comparison on n=1.","Final next steps are generic ('request a larger sample', 'Re-screen') and do not name the specific claims to request. The rationale text mentions the low-complexity claims, but the structured next_steps do not.","Only two example claims are cited (both low-complexity, with no dx detail beyond conditions), while the rationale names other claim IDs (C0084397, C0084474, C0084532, C0084637, C0085580, C0084535) that are not in cited_claim_ids.","'Of 1 documented 99215 claims' is awkward and 0 of 10 is a trivial finding; the draft is verbose for the evidence it has."]}
